scope: Source-level feasibility assessment only; no Dome Sculpt product modification, installation, runtime qualification or headset test
recommendation: Use ArmorPaint as a source donor for bounded painting/material/baking kernels behind Dome Sculpt-owned document/history and native FLTK/OpenXR controls. Do not substitute the whole stock application or its .arm project/packed layer representation for Dome Sculpt authority. A hosted paint engine is a substantial extraction, not an existing drop-in library.

findings.finding: Current main is native C with Iron engine and runtime Kong shader generation, not an old Haxe runtime. Build uses amake; normal Linux build does not require C23 embed, optional --embed requires clang19+.

Linux stock backend uses Vulkan plus X11. GTK native dialogs enabled by stock paint project. Supported current GPU backends are D3D12, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU; no OpenGL backend in current backend selection. No external-memory import/export or OpenXR path found by targeted source search. A GL/EGL Dome Sculpt consumer needs a port of shader kernels or newly implemented Vulkan sharing/synchronization.

Layers, masks, groups, fill materials, blending and per-channel toggles exist. GPU targets support UNORM8, float16 and float32. Hidden-layer records and raw layer buffers are saved. This is valuable painting functionality; claiming ArmorPaint lacks float/layer persistence would be incorrect.

The packed output semantics differ from Dome Sculpt all14: base RGB/opacity, tangent normal/material ID, AO/roughness/metal/height, plus transient R8 strength. Emission/subsurface are encoded through material-ID tagging rather than an independent physical RGB radiance and FLOAT coverage plane. float32 target support therefore does not supply Dome Sculpt physical-emission/source authority semantics.

The internal script layer API is coupled to global project/context, GPU begin/end, stock layer UI admission, and stock history. Painter/baker operate on global scene/render targets and frame notifications. Main includes implementation .c files into the app and owns startup/event loop. There is no assessed ready independently hosted multi-document library.

Undo uses rotating GPU texture slots and matching float formats; saving reads/compresses all GPU layers and temporarily mutates global app settings. This can inspire efficient GPU history, but must not replace immutable snapshots, detached transactions, generation/source validation, exact cancel and ordered worker saves without a new integration contract.

Upstream retains UV1 and skin blobs, so those features are not absent. Its paint mesh format uses normalized int16 vertex/UV arrays; .arm project schema is its own mesh/material/layer/skin/timeline model. The inspected import/export/schema does not implement Dome Sculpt original-node/accessor/MToon/VRM/morph/source-role authority roundtrip. Keep Dome Sculpt source and geometry authoritative; never transfer a full avatar roundtrip through ArmorPaint just to paint it.

bounded_next_milestone: Extract one shader/tool family, for example clone/blur or PBR material fill, into a UI-free module taking explicit mesh/UV, brush sample, immutable source textures and destination channel views; omit app/window/UI/project/history/plugin startup.

Prefer porting the extracted kernel to Dome Sculpt existing GL/compute resource ownership; if retaining Vulkan, first prove same-device external memory and synchronization without per-frame CPU texture readback before accepting that architecture.

Keep native sparse/all14/PBR/FLOAT/physical-emission/mask/layer/original-field archives, original coordinate/tangent roles, VRM/rig/morph graph, texture-set face membership and global undo/save entirely owned by Dome Sculpt.

Gate each adapted tool on independent channel/mask/FLOAT/source-role oracles, exact hidden-layer/native-save/restart/undo/cancel and posed/affine/VR controller tests. A flat PBR texture export is interchange only, not lossless native document migration.
verification: Clean source clone and pinned commit verified, root license hash verified, source APIs/build/backend/data/history paths inspected. No compile/runtime/performance/device or lossless interoperability claim.
